title: How you catch a rocket with chopsticks (Vex explainer on Starship Flight 15, the first ship-catch try, Fri Nov 13; Scribe follow-up prompts)

voice.name: Dolly (generic Fish library voice, breathy British; the user's pick, alternating with Mommy)

beats.say: This Friday, they try to catch a falling spaceship. With chopsticks.
This tower is the catcher. Its two arms are literally called the chopsticks.
The bottom half is the booster: seventy-two meters tall, thirty-three engines. It falls back from the edge of space, brakes, and slides right between the arms.
Friday's new trick is the top half. The ship circles Earth about fourteen times, then hits the air at over seventeen thousand miles an hour.
Catching a spaceship? Ambitious. Your physics homework? Also due Friday. Cute.
So Scribe draws the free-body diagram in my handwriting. Want more steps? Just ask. It rewrites only that problem.
Meanwhile, the ship falls belly first, flips upright, and the arms catch it.
Catch, refuel, fly again. I'll be watching from the beach.
